report.title: Three concurrent bugs: CSP blocks Ably token requests, LiveKit disconnects before connection establishes, Ably channel subscribed multiple times

bugs.title: CSP blocks Ably token endpoint (https://main.realtime.ably.net)
bugs.root_cause: The Content Security Policy in next.config.mjs includes https://*.ably.io and https://*.ably-realtime.com but does NOT include https://*.ably.net or wss://*.ably.net. Ably's SDK resolves to main.realtime.ably.net for token requests and fallback transports, which is a different subdomain pattern (.ably.net vs .ably.io / .ably-realtime.com). All three Ably domain patterns must be present.
error_messages: Connecting to 'https://main.realtime.ably.net/keys/RMZTfg.u3i6rw/requestToken?rnd=...' violates the following Content Security Policy directive: connect-src 'self' ws://localhost:* wss://localhost:* ws: wss: https://*.ably.io wss://*.ably.io https://*.ably-realtime.com wss://*.ably-realtime.com wss://*.livekit.cloud https://*.livekit.cloud

bugs.title: LiveKit room disconnects immediately — 'Client initiated disconnect' before WebSocket establishes
error_messages: Abort connection attempt due to user initiated disconnect
WebSocket connection to 'wss://trucknet-xzddcw8i.livekit.cloud/rtc/v1?access_token=...' failed: WebSocket is closed before the connection is established.
[useLiveKitRoom] connect failed: ConnectionError: Client initiated disconnect
bugs.root_cause: React 18 Strict Mode double-invokes useEffect in development — the component mounts, starts room.connect(), then immediately unmounts and remounts. The cleanup function of the first mount calls room.disconnect() while the WebSocket handshake is still in progress. The second mount starts a new connect() which also gets aborted by the same race. The fix requires: (1) a connection guard (isConnecting ref) to prevent concurrent connect calls, (2) an isMounted/aborted flag so cleanup does not call disconnect if connect never completed, and (3) using a stable Room instance with useRef instead of re-creating it on every render.

bugs.title: Ably channel subscribed multiple times — same event registered 3-4x per session
bugs.root_cause: useSocket hook is being called from multiple components simultaneously (e.g. layout.tsx, DriverMap, messages page all call useSocket independently). Each call creates its own subscription without checking if one already exists. Additionally, React Strict Mode double-fires effects, doubling the subscription count. Fix requires: (1) move the Ably Realtime instance and all channel subscriptions into a single React Context/Provider so there is exactly one instance per session, and (2) in the provider's useEffect cleanup, call channel.unsubscribe() for every registered listener before re-subscribing.

agent_prompt.role: You are a senior full-stack engineer working on TruckConnect, a Next.js 14 App Router application using Ably for real-time messaging and LiveKit for voice/video calls. You have full access to the codebase. Fix three bugs identified in BUG-002-A, BUG-002-B, and BUG-002-C below. Apply all fixes in the order listed. Do not introduce new dependencies.
agent_prompt.objective: Resolve all three bugs (CSP blocking Ably, LiveKit race-condition disconnect, Ably duplicate channel subscriptions) so that real-time messaging and voice/video calls work correctly on all devices.

fix_A.title: Add missing Ably .ably.net domains to Content Security Policy
instructions: Open next.config.mjs and locate the headers() function that sets the Content-Security-Policy header
Find the connect-src directive
The current connect-src includes https://*.ably.io, wss://*.ably.io, https://*.ably-realtime.com, wss://*.ably-realtime.com
Add the following two entries to connect-src immediately after the existing Ably entries: https://*.ably.net wss://*.ably.net
Also verify wss://*.livekit.cloud and https://*.livekit.cloud are present — if missing add them
Also add https://main.realtime.ably.net explicitly as a safety fallback

The final connect-src must contain ALL of the following Ably entries: https://*.ably.io wss://*.ably.io https://*.ably-realtime.com wss://*.ably-realtime.com https://*.ably.net wss://*.ably.net https://main.realtime.ably.net
Do not remove any existing entries
Restart the dev server after saving — CSP headers are set at build/startup time in Next.js
fix_A.code_template:
// In next.config.mjs headers() — connect-src value example:
const connectSrc = [
  "'self'",
  "ws://localhost:*",
  "wss://localhost:*",
  // Ably — all three domain patterns required
  "https://*.ably.io",
  "wss://*.ably.io",
  "https://*.ably-realtime.com",
  "wss://*.ably-realtime.com",
  "https://*.ably.net",
  "wss://*.ably.net",
  "https://main.realtime.ably.net",
  // LiveKit
  "wss://*.livekit.cloud",
  "https://*.livekit.cloud",
].join(' ');

fix_B.title: Fix LiveKit room connecting and immediately disconnecting (React StrictMode race condition)
instructions: Open hooks/useLiveKitRoom.ts

PROBLEM 1 — Room instance re-creation: Verify the Room object is created with useRef, NOT with useState or inline in the hook body. If it is created inline or with useState, move it to: const roomRef = useRef<Room | null>(null); if (!roomRef.current) { roomRef.current = new Room({ adaptiveStream: true, dynacast: true }); } const room = roomRef.current;

PROBLEM 2 — Concurrent connect calls: Add a connecting guard using useRef: const isConnectingRef = useRef(false). At the start of the connect logic inside useEffect, check: if (isConnectingRef.current) return; isConnectingRef.current = true; — and reset it in the finally block: isConnectingRef.current = false;

PROBLEM 3 — Cleanup calling disconnect on inflight connection: Add an abort flag inside the useEffect: let aborted = false; — In the cleanup function return () => { aborted = true; room.disconnect(); }; — After await room.connect(liveKitUrl, token) completes, check: if (aborted) { room.disconnect(); return; } — This ensures that if StrictMode already cleaned up before connect finished, we immediately disconnect the now-orphaned connection

PROBLEM 4 — Token fetch triggering re-render loop: The token fetch must NOT be in a useEffect with dependencies that change after the fetch (e.g. putting token in state and listing it as a dep). Use a ref for the token: const tokenRef = useRef<string | null>(null). Fetch the token once inside the connect effect and store it in tokenRef.current before passing to room.connect()

The corrected useLiveKitRoom hook connect effect must follow this exact sequence: (1) check isConnectingRef guard, (2) set guard to true, (3) fetch token from /api/calls/token/${roomName}, (4) check aborted flag before proceeding, (5) call room.connect(liveKitUrl, token), (6) check aborted flag again after connect, (7) reset guard in finally, (8) catch errors and call onError callback

In app/(protected)/calls/[roomName]/page.tsx: verify the component does NOT call room.disconnect() in a useEffect cleanup that runs during normal navigation-within-the-call-page re-renders. The disconnect should only happen on explicit user action (end call button) or when the component fully unmounts (navigating away from /calls)

fix_C.title: Fix Ably duplicate channel subscriptions — move to singleton Context Provider
instructions: DIAGNOSIS: Run a search in the codebase for all files that call useSocket() — list every component and hook that imports and calls it. The duplicate subscriptions mean multiple component trees each independently create Ably channel subscriptions for the same events.
SOLUTION: Refactor useSocket into a Context-based singleton pattern:
STEP 1 — Create a SocketContext: In hooks/useSocket.ts (or a new file components/SocketProvider.tsx), define: const SocketContext = createContext<SocketContextValue | null>(null)

STEP 2 — Create SocketProvider component: This component holds the single Ably.Realtime instance in a useRef. In its useEffect it creates the instance once, subscribes to 'user:{clientId}' and 'stress:alerts' channels, and stores event listeners in a Map<eventName, Set<handler>>. The cleanup returns channel.unsubscribe() + realtime.close().

STEP 3 — on() and off() methods: Instead of calling channel.subscribe() directly each time on() is called (which stacks subscriptions), maintain an internal listener registry (Map<eventName, Set<handler>>). When the Ably channel message arrives, iterate the Set and call each registered handler. on() adds to the Set, off() removes from it. This means Ably itself only ever has ONE subscription per event name, regardless of how many components call on().

STEP 4 — Add SocketProvider to Providers.tsx: Wrap the children with <SocketProvider> inside the existing Providers component, alongside SessionProvider. Ensure it is INSIDE SessionProvider so it can read the session.

STEP 5 — Remove all direct Ably.Realtime instantiation from useSocket.ts body: The hook body should now just call useContext(SocketContext) and throw if null (i.e. used outside provider). All components that call useSocket() will now share the single instance from the Provider.

STEP 6 — Verify React StrictMode safety: The useEffect in SocketProvider must handle double-invocation. Use the standard pattern: inside useEffect, create Ably instance; in cleanup, call realtime.close() and clear the listener Map. On second mount, a fresh instance is created cleanly.

verification_steps.action: Restart the dev server after applying all three fixes: npm run dev
Open browser DevTools → Console. Verify ZERO CSP errors for ably.net or livekit.cloud domains
Open DevTools → Console. Verify each Ably event (text_message_received, voice_message_received) appears subscribed EXACTLY ONCE, not multiple times
Initiate a voice call. In the Console verify NO 'Client initiated disconnect' or 'Abort connection attempt' errors appear
Confirm the LiveKit WebSocket connects successfully — look for the room 'connected' event in the console log from useLiveKitRoom
Send a text message and verify it arrives in real-time without duplicate delivery (which would indicate duplicate subscriptions are still active)
Open DevTools → Network → WS. Verify exactly ONE WebSocket connection to realtime.ably.net and ONE to livekit.cloud during an active call

constraints: Do not downgrade React or disable StrictMode as a workaround — fix the actual race condition
Do not hardcode the Ably API key on the client — always use authUrl: '/api/auth/ably-token'
Do not add new npm packages — use the existing livekit-client and ably packages
The SocketProvider must be placed INSIDE NextAuth SessionProvider in Providers.tsx so useSession() works inside it
Do not change the Ably channel naming convention (user:{userId} and stress:alerts)
The Room instance in useLiveKitRoom must never be recreated between renders — use useRef
